statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Weekend venue closure with no live Nasdaq-100 price path; Tail remains far below the block threshold while Stress stays elevated on hawkish rate repricing, Hormuz energy risk and a fresh Iranian escalation statement.
recommendation: Conditions map to EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Conditional risk is concentrated in the narrow 22:00-02:00 UTC futures-reopen window rather than across the session; existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Iran drops proportionate response ahead of a thin 22:00 UTC reopen into a US Labor Day holiday
body: CME equity index futures have been closed since Friday 21:00 UTC, so no live Nasdaq-100 price path is observable at this assessment. The last verified tape remains Friday September 4: ^NDX closed 29,544.15 (+0.21%) inside a 29,440.15-29,655.22 range, a mid-range finish with no session-extreme hold, and VIX ended at 14.53 after a 13.80-14.58 day range. The S&P 500 fell 0.38% to 7,718.41 and the Nasdaq Composite 0.29% to 26,506.99 after the August employment report printed 162,000 payrolls against roughly 56,000 consensus, with prior months revised up a combined 55,000 and unemployment steady at 4.1%. That repricing lifted odds of a 25bp hike at the September 15-16 FOMC to 58.4% from 49.4% a day earlier; H.15 still shows the September 3 readings of 2Y 4.34% and 10Y 4.77%. The pre-FOMC communications blackout began September 5 and runs through September 17, which removes Fed-speaker headlines from the entire forecast window. The one new verified development since the previous assessment is verbal rather than kinetic: at roughly 10:49 UTC Iran's Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf stated that the era of proportionate responses is over and that further action against Iran would draw a faster, heavier and more painful reply. That follows Saturday's exchange in which US forces disabled or destroyed Iranian tankers after IRGC missile launches toward US warships, and the IRGC then claimed strikes on US-affiliated vessels and tankers in Hormuz. Brent settled $96.28 and WTI $91.48, weekly gains of 7.6% and nearly 10%. The combination lifts Stress by three points to 57. The strategy-relevant failure mode requires an observed no-retracement price path, and none exists: Friday closed mid-range, VIX stayed below 15, and internals were mixed with semiconductors firm while several megacaps fell. Tail therefore stays low at 5 and maps to EA_ON. Conditional risk concentrates in the 22:00-02:00 UTC reopen window, where the thinnest depth of the week meets an explicit escalation signal issued hours earlier and a Monday Labor Day closure that removes the cash session normally available to absorb a weekend gap; that single reopen hour is the only slot in the window carrying a conditional caution mapping.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available. Tail held flat at 4-5 with EA_ON and green throughout, while Stress ranged from 39 during Saturday's European hours to a 57 peak around the Saturday evening tanker exchange, then oscillated between 52 and 56 across the remaining weekend closure. Confidence stayed in an 84-86 band and dominant mode was normal for every hour.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours cover eleven further closed hours, the 22:00 UTC futures reopen, and an Asian and European session on a US Labor Day holiday. Conditional Tail stays inside the low band except for the single reopen hour, which reaches 20 and maps to WATCH where two days of Hormuz escalation and a fresh Iranian statement meet the thinnest depth of the week, before decaying toward 8 as two-way discovery is assumed to resume. Stress peaks near 67 at the reopen on the combined rates and energy backdrop before unwinding toward 53. No US macro release falls inside the window and the Fed is in its pre-FOMC blackout; the next scheduled checkpoints are the NFIB survey on September 8, August PPI on September 10 and August CPI on September 11, ahead of the September 15-16 FOMC.
